enumeration.method: Independent font-aware enumeration of main-text pages 1–36, visually checked on all five theorem pages. Actual headings use SFBX1200. Appendix boundary inspected by title-only clip on page 37.

source_notes: Pinned arXiv:2211.10203v2 has a margin date of 21 November 2022 and title-page date of 18 November 2022. Equivalence to the final journal typesetting is not asserted.
Main text and references end on page 36. Numbered Section 5 is main text, while the actual attached supplement starts on page 37. Supplement mathematics is excluded.

Barred Sigma is the unconditional covariance; unbarred Sigma_t is the conditional covariance. Matrix/vector Latin symbols are bold upright. The iid reference is coupled through the same z_t, not a newly independent innovation sample.
The source defines the iid comparator for t=1,...,T but defines its sample covariance using t=1,...,n. The main-text passage does not identify T with n.
Assumption 1 requires a nonzero limiting population law and an upper spectral-norm bound. It does not impose positive definiteness of every population covariance or a positive lower eigenvalue bound.
The scalar eta uses sqrt(p(1-a-b)) inside a minimum with one. The coefficient denominator is 1-a-b, not its square root.
Theorem 2 asserts only a positive gap between expected empirical spectral second moments. The heavier-tail prose is not strengthened to a stochastic-order or Levy-distance theorem.
The QMLE is printed as argmax of the positive Gaussian contrast, without the usual negative sign. Preserve its optimization direction and objective literally.
The QMLE uses a randomly selected single coordinate. Remark 1 discusses pooling only as a practical alternative; a pooled estimator is not substituted into the theorem dependencies.

The QMLE parameter domain constrains the unconditional marginal variance by delta<=bar-sigma^2<C, while Assumption 1 allows singular population covariances. The main-text construction does not specify how the selected coordinate is guaranteed to satisfy that lower bound.

The main text does not specify the QMLE initialization, all candidate conditional variance recursions at finite sample boundaries, or a measurable tie-selection rule. The cited external algorithmic details remain unresolved.
The source calls P_t a projection matrix, but its formula is a weighted covariance matrix plus an identity term. Idempotence or orthogonality is not inferred from the name.

The projection uses M_p presample returns when t is small. The main-text definition does not detail how those observations or an initialization are supplied. M_p is an integer lag count with the displayed asymptotic growth.
The covariance estimators are uncentered outer-product averages divided by n. No estimated-mean subtraction or n-1 normalization is inserted.
Equation (2.9) uses y, while Theorem 4 equation (2.12) uses y^{-1} twice. Both source formulas are retained rather than reconciled by editing.
The generalized ESD (2.10) divides by tr(g(bar-Sigma)), but its generalized transform (2.11) divides by p. They are not silently treated as the same normalized transform.

For a merely bounded g, the generalized ESD denominator can be zero and the weights need not be nonnegative. The source does not add positivity or nonzero-trace hypotheses; equation (2.11) itself does not require this denominator.

Theorem 4 restricts g on the support interval of the limiting H but applies g to finite-dimensional population eigenvalues. It does not explicitly specify a global extension of g or require every such eigenvalue to lie in that interval.
Theorem 4 gives convergence for each z in the upper half-plane, without uniform-in-z or almost-sure quantification. Its limit is bound inline and is not separately inventoried as another Theorem.
The clipping threshold L is called a large constant without a quantitative lower bound here. Tau labels clipping, not a separate threshold value. Eigenvectors are preserved.

The Ledoit–Wolf (2015) nonlinear shrinkage algorithm is invoked by reference; its complete numerical construction is not in this main-text passage. The census records an unresolved external definition and does not substitute the oracle formula.

The oracle zero-eigenvalue branch uses the companion boundary value check-m_{underline F}(0) only when y>1. The printed otherwise branch also covers boundary cases not separately analyzed here, including zero eigenvalues with y=1.
The oracle nonzero branch uses an ordinary squared denominator without absolute-value bars. Complex boundary values can make this distinction substantive, so the source formula is not repaired.

Only the F subscript is underlined in the companion m_{underline F}. The source boundary-value definition writes check-m without an F subscript on the left, despite using indexed boundary values in (2.13).

The companion expression uses an indicator printed with braces around [0,infinity). This notation is preserved. Existence/nonvanishing of all boundary values used in the oracle is not separately stipulated in the main-text definition.

Theorem 5 inherits the assumptions of Theorem 4, including its g condition, but not its conclusion. Its metric is a dimension-normalized Frobenius difference from the oracle, not consistency to the unconditional covariance itself.

External results on QMLE rates, MP limits and oracle optimality are cited as justifications. They are not additional inventoried Theorems or proof-derived dependencies. QuEST population-spectrum consistency is Corollary 1 and is excluded from the Theorem inventory.
recorded_checks: Pinned source title, both authors, 49-page count, arXiv version, two printed dates and PDF SHA checked. Fresh extraction matches every archived main-text page byte for byte.

Independent font-aware enumeration finds exactly five Theorems and one numbered Assumption. Four ordinary-font theorem mentions and the Section 5 proof heading are excluded. The actual supplement starts on page 37.
All five complete original statements remain unchanged from the independently validated inventory. Their hypotheses, endpoint quantifiers and formulas were checked on pages 7, 8, 10, 12 and 13.

All four parts of Assumption 1, the dynamic/iid return coupling, sample covariance normalization and covariance-bar typography are preserved. The extra support and function restrictions in Theorem 4 are not strengthened.
The source eta scaling, distinct regimes and expected second-moment gap are checked. Theorem 2 does not gain an unstated stochastic-order or Levy-distance conclusion.

Main-text construction review covers the marginal GARCH variance, random-coordinate QMLE and domain, full projection formula, inverse-square-root returns and adjusted covariance. The positive argmax criterion is preserved.
Stieltjes and generalized resolvent formulas, the matrix function g, clipped eigenvalues, NLS invocation and oracle branches are checked against pages 10–13, including enlarged oracle/QMLE crops.
The inverse-y discrepancy, trace normalization mismatch, ordinary squared oracle denominator, underlined companion F and unindexed boundary-value shorthand remain recorded as source issues.

Independent traversal verifies 30 direct uses and 61 related connections. Theorem 5 inherits the hypotheses of Theorem 4 but not its generalized-transform conclusion, and its oracle does not depend on the numerical NLS algorithm.

All 24 source passages have original terminology, faithful source kinds, meaningful selectors and same-paper explanations. Twelve auxiliary passages preserve unnamed/local definitions and contextual formulas; external NLS details remain explicitly unresolved.
export_note: Public summary of the recorded source review. Local paths, execution metadata and unbundled working-file references are omitted. Original statements and interface relationships are in the aggregate census. A recorded review is not a formal proof certificate.
